sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: RGD cluster nucleation assay: EGFP-tagged ITGB3 nucleated RGD clusters at 15 and 60 min, indistinguishable from positive controls — extracellular function preserved.
sites.rationale: ITGB3 is a Type I single-pass transmembrane protein with exactly one extracellular terminus — the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 27 (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 26) — and an intracellular C-terminus (residues 745–788). L1 reports a full-length, membrane-anchored EGFP-tagged ITGB3 construct in CHO-B2 cells with preserved RGD cluster nucleation, confirming surface expression and extracellular function. Because no residue or loop is named, the topology_derived rule places the tag after residue 26 (the sole extracellular terminus). Confidence is low because the paper does not explicitly state whether EGFP is N- or C-terminal; a C-terminal EGFP would be intracellular and would still permit surface expression and RGD binding, making the extracellular assignment uncertain. Full-length EGFP-tagged ITGB3 expressed in CHO-B2 cells (mammalian, membrane-anchored); no residue or loop position is named in the paper.

sources.claim: A) EGFP‐tagged integrin β6, β5, and β3 expressed in CHO‐B2 cells nucleate RGD clusters in 15 and 60‐min.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) is available. It reports EGFP-tagged full-length ITGB3 in CHO-B2 cells with RGD cluster nucleation preserved, but names neither a residue nor a loop. The topology_derived rule assigns the tag to the mature N-terminus (insert_after_residue=26) because that is the sole extracellular terminus of this Type I TM protein. Confidence is low because C-terminal EGFP (intracellular, residues 745–788) is equally consistent with the reported phenotype; the paper does not disambiguate. No other ledger lines exist to support additional sites. The intracellular C-terminus (residue 788) is noted in other_positions as a plausible alternative location for the EGFP that would not constitute a surface tag.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal EGFP fusion is equally consistent with the L1 data (surface expression and RGD cluster nucleation do not require an extracellular tag); if EGFP is C-terminal it is intracellular and not a surface tag site.
